headline: The early table has a shape, but not a verdict
standfirst: Trevor Hash brings the league's highest score into Week 2, while the reigning champion is already chasing a response against JD Daley.

source_trace.description: Live ESPN board snapshot; Week 2 remains in progress

lead.title: The early table has a shape, but not a verdict
lead.body: Trevor Hash owns the early headline after a 192.56-point Week 1 and a 1–0 start. Bryan Hunt and Vincent Cannarozzi are also above 150 points, giving the first table a clear front edge. The complication is timing: Week 2 is still live, and early-season standings are signals rather than sentences. The most interesting pressure point is at the other end of the board, where reigning champion Thomas Speer is 0–1 and currently trailing JD Daley in the week's live matchup. One result will not rewrite the title race, but it can change the conversation.

matchup.whyItMatters: The reigning champion is trying to avoid an 0–2 opening while Daley is looking to turn a narrow Week 1 loss into an immediate response.
matchup.history: This is an early-season pressure game, not a declared rivalry. The result matters because both managers began the season with a loss.

pressure.title: Under pressure: the reigning champion
pressure.body: The early pressure is about the scoreboard, not the résumé. Speer's title defense began with a loss, and the live Week 2 matchup is another test. A comeback would turn the opening stumble into background noise; another loss would make the defense of the crown a real weekly storyline.

surprise.title: Biggest surprise: the scoring gap is already loud
surprise.body: Team Hash's 192.56 points in Week 1 are 90.32 points higher than Kyle Fowler's total. That is an early scoring signal, not a season forecast, but it explains why Hash currently leads both the table and the conversation.

recordWatch.title: Record to watch: Hash has the first benchmark
recordWatch.body: Trevor Hash's 192.56 points are the first major scoring benchmark of Szn 10. Week 2's live board will show whether the early leader can add another statement before the archive starts to separate contenders from noise.
